mainKeyword: cordless pole hedge trimmer with battery and charger
guideTitle: Best Cordless Pole Hedge Trimmers with Battery and Charger (2026)
metaTitle: Best Cordless Pole Hedge Trimmers, Battery Kits
metaDescription: Six cordless pole hedge trimmer kits that ship with battery and charger, compared on pack size, blade length, pole reach and what each kit really includes.
expertTake: The Alloyman 16 inch kit with two 4.0Ah packs is the best-balanced complete package, and the Black+Decker is the safe brand choice with one pack. The YDlawn 22 inch is the pick for a long blade. Skip every kit with a single small pack if your hedges take more than twenty minutes.
introParagraphs: A complete kit means you can cut the day the box arrives, but the contents vary more than the product photos suggest. One kit ships with two large packs and a fast charger, while another gives you one small pack and a slow one.

Because a pole tool is held up in the air, runtime and weight pull against each other, and the pack you get decides how long each session lasts. This guide reads each kit by what is in the box and what that means for real work.

products.name: Alloyman 20V MAX 16 in. Telescoping Pole Hedge Trimmer, Two 4.0Ah Batteries
products.description:
This kit gets the contents right. Two 4.0Ah batteries and a charger come in the box, which is roughly double the energy of the 2.0Ah kits, and the 16 inch hardened steel dual-action blade is listed to cut 3/4 inch at 1,400 strokes per minute. That capacity is generous for a 16 inch pole head.

The pole extends up to 8 feet and folds shorter for storage, and the listing gives the weight as 8 pounds, which is on the heavy side but normal when two large packs are involved. The ergonomic non-slip rubber grip helps with control. It does not have the extras of the TaskStar, such as a strap, so it relies on your arm strength.

What you get is endurance. With two 4.0Ah packs you can work through a long hedge in two sessions without waiting for a recharge, and you can rest while the first pack refills. Keep the telescopic joint clean and store the packs indoors. A smaller brand means you should check the warranty, but in terms of what is in the box it is the strongest kit of the six. When you work through a hedge, run the first pack until the tool slows, then swap and let the first one rest before recharging, since lithium cells charge more happily once they have cooled.
products.bestFor: Long or numerous hedges where battery capacity is the limit.
pros: Two 4.0Ah packs give long working time
3/4 in. cut capacity on a 16 inch blade
Telescopic pole up to 8 ft that folds short
cons: 8 lb is heavy with no strap

products.name: Black+Decker 20V MAX 18 in. Cordless Pole Hedge Trimmer Kit with Battery and Charger
products.description:
Black+Decker's kit is the conventional answer. It ships with one 20V MAX battery and a charger, an 18 inch dual-action blade and a head that pivots through five positions over 180 degrees. The adjustable length reaches around 6.5 feet, shorter than the telescopic Alloyman, but enough for most garden hedges.

What the kit does not have is battery depth. One pack means a recharge before you carry on, so plan the job in two parts or buy a spare. The advantage is that spares, chargers and replacement parts are widely stocked, which matters five years from now.

At 7.7 pounds, it is about the same weight as the Alloyman despite carrying a smaller pack, so the weight is in the shaft and head. The pivot joint is the part to keep clean. Wipe the blades after use and store the pack indoors, and the tool should serve for years. If a second battery is needed, buying one from the same line is simple, and it will fit other 20V MAX tools you may add later. That flexibility is worth more than a bigger pack in the box if you expect to build up a tool collection.
products.bestFor: Buyers who prefer a known brand and easy spare parts.
pros: Battery and charger included from a known brand
cons: Only one battery in the kit
Shorter reach than the telescopic models

products.name: YDlawn 20V 22 in. Cordless Pole Hedge Trimmer, 8 ft Pole, Two 4.0Ah Batteries

specList.label: Pole
specList.value: 8 ft telescopic, up to 15 ft reach claimed

products.description:
The YDlawn has the longest blade in the guide at 22 inches, so it covers a wide swath per pass, and it comes with two 4.0Ah batteries and a fast charger. The listing claims up to 2 hours of runtime across both packs, which is a best-case figure and is plausible only on light growth.

The 15 foot reach is the user's height plus the 8 foot pole, so the pole itself is 8 feet and standing reach on a hedge top is nearer 12 to 13 feet. The 22 inch blade is cut to 5/8 inch, a smaller capacity than the Alloyman's 3/4 inch, so it trades power for width.

A 22 inch head is a lot to hold out at the end of a pole, and tip weight is the concern. Rest the pole against your hip when you can, and clean sap off the blade after each session. If you have a long, flat hedge top that is only lightly overgrown, the extra blade width will save you time. It is a poor choice for stems near the 5/8 inch limit, because a wide blade with a small gap bogs down sooner than a narrow blade with the same gap. Keep your passes slow and steady, and let the blade, not the pole, do the work.
products.bestFor: Long, flat hedge tops with soft growth.
pros: 22 inch blade is the widest here
Two 4.0Ah packs and a fast charger
cons: 5/8 in. capacity is lower than the Alloyman
Long blade adds tip weight on a pole

products.name: TaskStar 20V 16 in. Cordless Pole Hedge Trimmer Kit with Shoulder Strap, 8.5 ft
products.description:
TaskStar sells a kit built around comfort rather than raw runtime. A shoulder strap and a second handle spread the load across your body, and the head turns through six positions, so you can hold a flat angle on the top without bending your neck.

The pole extends up to 8.5 feet and the blade is 16 inches, which keeps the tip weight lower than on the 22 inch YDlawn. It comes with a battery and charger, but the listing is less specific than the Alloyman about pack size, so check the amp-hours before you buy if runtime is your priority.

The strap clips take the strain, so inspect them each season. For anyone who has found that a bare pole tool is too tiring to use for more than ten minutes, this kit is the most practical way to keep going. Set the strap length before you extend the pole, since changing it overhead is awkward. Test the strap clips by tugging them hard once, as a failed clip with the blade running is the one real hazard of this design.
products.bestFor: Users who value comfort and load sharing over raw runtime.
pros: 16 inch blade keeps tip weight low
cons: Pack size is less clearly stated

products.name: Alloyman 20V 20 in. 2-in-1 Pole and Handheld Hedge Trimmer, Two 4.0Ah Batteries
products.description:
The detachable pole makes this a two-tool kit. Remove the extension and you have a 20 inch handheld trimmer, add it back and you can reach 6.5 to 8.5 feet. A 20 inch hardened steel dual-action blade cuts to 7/10 inch, which lands between the YDlawn at 5/8 inch and the Alloyman 16 inch at 3/4 inch.

Two 4.0Ah batteries and a charger are in the kit, so the energy is the same as on the other Alloyman. The joint between the pole and the head is the weak point, because a detachable pole flexes more than a one-piece telescoping shaft, and it reduces precision at full extension.

For a yard with low borders and a few tall hedges, the 2-in-1 saves buying twice. Clean the joint contacts after use and store the head and the pole together. When you use it as a handheld, remember that a 20 inch blade is a long reach for one hand, so grip it with both. Check that the locking collar clicks fully home each time you reassemble it.
products.bestFor: A yard that mixes low borders and a few tall hedges.
cons: Detachable joint flexes at full reach

products.name: Craftsman V20 18 in. Cordless Pole Hedge Trimmer Kit with Battery and Charger
products.description:
Craftsman quotes up to 11 feet of reach, the greatest of any kit here, though as with other pole tools that figure includes your arms. The 18 inch blade is dual-action and cuts to 3/4 inch, and the head pivots 180 degrees in five positions.

The kit includes a V20 battery and charger, but a single pack means one session at a time. The platform is the draw, since V20 batteries are used by many Craftsman tools and are easy to buy as spares. Next to the Alloyman, you give up battery depth and gain a recognisable platform.

A long shaft flexes at full extension, so keep the head angle near 30 to 45 degrees and do not extend more than you need. Store it collapsed and keep the pack indoors. If you cut mostly at the top of tall privet, the extra reach is useful, but a ladder-free setup also needs firm, level footing under your own feet. Buy a spare V20 pack early, since a single battery is the limit on this kit.
products.bestFor: Craftsman V20 owners with tall hedges.
pros: V20 spare packs are easy to find
cons: Reach claim includes the user's arms

buyingCriteria.explanation: What is in the box sets how long you can work. The Alloyman and YDlawn kits ship with two 4.0Ah batteries, while the Black+Decker and Craftsman kits include a single pack. Two large packs mean you can work, rest and swap without waiting.

A slow charger keeps you waiting between sessions. The YDlawn lists a fast charger with its two 4.0Ah packs and claims up to 2 hours of runtime. Check charge time before you assume two packs will keep you cutting continuously. A 4.0Ah pack on a basic charger can take several hours, and that gap decides whether the second pack is a convenience or a necessity.

The YDlawn blade is 22 inches, the Alloyman 20 inches in the 2-in-1 and 16 inches in the telescopic. Longer blades cut more per pass but load the end of the pole. For most users 16 to 18 inches is easier to hold.
The Alloyman 16 inch and Craftsman list 3/4 inch, the Alloyman 2-in-1 lists 7/10 inch and the YDlawn 5/8 inch. Capacity depends on tooth gap, not blade length.
A one-piece telescoping shaft is stiffer than a detachable one. The Alloyman 2-in-1 trades some rigidity for the ability to become a handheld. Flex at full extension lowers control.
The YDlawn claims 15 feet and the Craftsman 11 feet, both including your own reach. Subtract roughly 3 to 5 feet to find the pole's real standing height.

faq.q: What should a pole kit include?
faq.a: At minimum a battery, charger and the tool. Better kits add a second battery and a fast charger, as with the Alloyman and YDlawn.

faq.q: How big a battery do I need?
faq.a: For hedges over 20 minutes, aim for 4.0Ah packs or two packs. Smaller packs run out before a long hedge is done.
No. The YDlawn pole is 8 feet and the 15 feet includes your own height. Real standing reach is closer to 12 feet.

faq.q: Do I need a fast charger?
faq.a: It helps if you only own one spare. A fast charger refills the first pack while you use the second.

From 5/8 to 3/4 inch depending on the model. Thicker stems need a pole saw. Forcing a blade through a stem past its rated gap is the fastest way to strip gears and dull teeth, so switch tools instead of pushing harder.

faq.q: Can I use the battery in other tools?
faq.a: Only within the same platform. Black+Decker and Craftsman packs run other tools in their ranges, while the others are mostly specific to the kit. Before you buy, check whether a spare pack for the platform is sold separately and at what price, because a one-off battery you cannot replace turns a good tool into a short-lived one.
